from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The warden marks a secret square on the board.",
            "Coins cover the board randomly, heads or tails.",
            "One prisoner flips a coin to signal the square."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Prisoner's Dilemma", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a text label "Prisoner's Dilemma" in #FFFFFF at center.
        label = Text("Prisoner's Dilemma", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'C3')
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Fade in two circle representations for prisoners in #4DA6FF.
        alice = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#4DA6FF", fill_opacity=0.6)
        bob = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#4DA6FF", fill_opacity=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(alice, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(bob, 'B5')
        self.play(FadeIn(alice), FadeIn(bob))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#4DA6FF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw a decision payoff matrix with labels in #FFFF00.
        matrix = Matrix([[r"T", r"S"], [r"P", r"R"]], h_buff=0.8, v_buff=0.8).set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(matrix, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(matrix))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Prerequisite: Binary State and XOR", [
            "Represent each coin as a binary bit.",
            "XOR parity acts as our checksum.",
            "Parity maps states to coordinate vectors."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        bit_0 = MathTex("0", color="#4DA6FF").scale(2)
        bit_1 = MathTex("1", color="#4DA6FF").scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(bit_0, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(bit_1, 'B5')
        self.play(FadeIn(bit_0), FadeIn(bit_1))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#4DA6FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        xor_expr = MathTex("0", r"\oplus", "1", "=", "1", color=WHITE)
        xor_expr[0].set_color("#4DA6FF")
        xor_expr[2].set_color("#4DA6FF")
        xor_expr[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(xor_expr, 'D3')
        self.play(Write(xor_expr))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        parity_result = MathTex("P = 0 \\oplus 1 = 1", color="#FF00FF").scale(1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(parity_result, 'E3')
        self.play(FadeIn(parity_result))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Total parity points to the secret square.",
            "Flip one coin to force the parity.",
            "Bob reads parity to find the square.",
            "The secret is encoded in the parity.",
            "Success is guaranteed by simple XOR math."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Strategy: Parity as a Pointer", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        parity_bits = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5, color=WHITE) for _ in range(4)])
        self.place_at_grid(parity_bits, 'B2')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#4DA6FF"))
        # Visualize prisoners standing in a line
        self.play(Create(parity_bits))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Show bits being passed forward as parity sum
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid['B2'], end=self.grid['B5'], color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        # Reveal how parity identifies the hidden bit
        indicator = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(indicator, 'B5')
        self.play(Create(indicator))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Bridging to Information Theory", 
                          ["The board acts as an information channel.", 
                           "Parity protects against transmission errors.", 
                           "We lose no information during encoding."])
        
        # Animation Elements

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.place_at_grid(parity_bit, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(parity_bit))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.place_at_grid(error_indicator, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(error_indicator))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        text = Text("Robust Information Transfer", font_size=24, color="#FF00FF")

        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Impossible Chessboard: Decoding Information Theory

sections.title: Introduction: The Prisoner's Dilemma
sections.content: Introduce the challenge: A prison warden places a 64-square chessboard covered with coins (Heads/Tails) randomly. One square is marked 'the secret square.' Two prisoners must communicate: one looks at the board and flips exactly one coin to signal the secret square's location to the other. How can they guarantee survival?
sections.example: Visual: Two characters, Alice and Bob, standing before a 8x8 grid of glowing coins.

sections.title: Mathematical Prerequisite: Binary State and XOR
sections.content: Explain the concept of bit-parity. Any state on the board can be represented as a sequence of bits (0 for Tails, 1 for Heads). Introduce XOR (exclusive OR) as a way to calculate a 'checksum' of a set of bits, which is essential for error detection.
sections.example: Visual: A simple 2x2 grid showing how XORing the positions of 'Heads' results in a coordinate vector.

sections.title: The Strategy: Parity as a Pointer
sections.content: Explain the core solution: The board's total XOR sum acts as a 'coordinate pointer.' By flipping exactly one coin, Alice forces the total parity of the board to match the secret square's binary coordinate. Bob simply calculates the current parity to 'read' the secret square.
sections.example: Visual: An animation showing a parity vector shifting to point at square (3, 5) as a single coin flips from 0 to 1.

sections.title: Bridging to Information Theory
sections.content: Connect the puzzle to Hamming Codes and Information Theory. Explain that the chessboard is an information channel; by using parity, the prisoners effectively compress the board's state information to transmit the 'secret' coordinate with zero redundancy loss.
sections.example: Visual: A data transmission diagram replacing the coins with data packets, showing parity bits protecting the signal.

sections.title: Conclusion and Real-World Impact
sections.content: Summarize how this seemingly impossible puzzle illustrates the fundamental limits of information density. Mention its application in ECC (Error Correction Code) memory used in modern computers.
sections.example: Visual: A server rack icon fading into the chessboard, illustrating that the math protecting the prisoners is the same math protecting our digital files.
